harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured a persistent UFW host firewall on node1 via an Ansible playbook run from node2 (the control node, identified as the only node with ansible/ansible-playbook installed). The firewall's default incoming policy is reject, default outgoing is allow, with explicit allow rules for TCP 22 (SSH) and TCP 8080; UFW is enabled and set to start at boot. Functional tests confirmed SSH and 8080 reachable while an unrelated port (9999) was actively refused. Completed the mandatory restart-evidence protocol on both node1 and node2: captured healthy baselines, restarted each node one at a time via `systemctl reboot`, confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and verified post-restart recovery (UFW state/rules persisted on node1; ansible tooling, playbook, and SSH connectivity to node1 recovered on node2, with a fully idempotent playbook re-run as final proof).
actions_performed: Inspected node1 and node2 to identify node2 as the configured Ansible control node
Fixed a pre-existing issue on node1 where sshd could not start due to missing host keys (dpkg-reconfigure openssh-server) and restarted ssh
Wired CLUSTER_SSH_PRIVKEY/PUBKEY for passwordless root SSH from node2 to node1
Wrote Ansible inventory (/root/ansible/inventory.ini) and playbook (/root/ansible/host-firewall.yml) on node2 using the community.general.ufw module
Ran the playbook to install ufw, set default incoming policy to reject and outgoing to allow, allow tcp/22 and tcp/8080, enable ufw, and enable the ufw systemd unit
Adjusted default incoming policy from 'deny' to 'reject' to match the task's explicit 'rejecting' wording, and re-ran the playbook
Functionally verified from node2: SSH works, an ephemeral HTTP server on 8080 was reachable (curl 200), and an unrelated port (9999) was refused
Captured boot_id/boot-time baselines on node1 and node2, restarted node1 via systemctl reboot, confirmed changed boot_id, verified UFW state/rules persisted and functional tests still passed

Restarted node2 via systemctl reboot, confirmed changed boot_id, verified ansible tooling, playbook file, SSH key, and SSH connectivity to node1 recovered, and re-ran the playbook to confirm full idempotency (changed=0)

evidence.requirement: Baseline health before any restart (node1 firewall, node2 ansible control capability)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id/boot-time plus ufw active/enabled state with correct rules on node1, and ansible/playbook presence on node2, prior to any restart.

evidence.requirement: Ansible playbook implements persistent UFW firewall permitting SSH and 8080, rejecting other inbound traffic
evidence.summary: ansible-playbook runs succeeded (ok=8, changed=1/3) and ufw status/rules files confirm default reject incoming, allow outgoing, with explicit allow for 22/tcp and 8080/tcp, enabled at boot via /etc/default/ufw and systemd.

evidence.requirement: Functional proof firewall permits SSH/8080 and rejects unrelated inbound
evidence.summary: From node2: SSH succeeded, curl to 8080 (test HTTP server) returned 200, and curl to unrelated port 9999 was actively refused (connection refused, not timeout).

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; node1 unreachable mid-reboot; boot_id changed from 242af11e... to 6a97cfef... with advanced boot time; post-restart ufw active/enabled with identical persisted rules; functional SSH and unrelated-port-rejection re-verified after restart.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; node2 unreachable/connection-reset mid-reboot; boot_id changed from 416c5cf5... to 29e21af9... with advanced boot time; post-restart ansible, playbook file, SSH key, and SSH connectivity to node1 all recovered, and a re-run of the playbook was fully idempotent (changed=0), proving node1's firewall state is intact and node2's control-node role is fully functional.
